task.title: Draw shapes and reuse them
task.shortdesc: You draw with seven shape elements. You can group shapes, move and turn them, and define a shape once to draw it many times.

info.p: Each shape element has attributes for its position and size. All the numbers are in user units, which are CSS pixels unless you change the scale with a viewBox.

row.entry: x and y for the top left corner, width and height, and rx and ry for rounded corners. When you write only one radius, the other one has the same value.
cx and cy for the center, and r for the radius.
cx and cy for the center, and rx and ry for the two radii.
x1 and y1 for the start, and x2 and y2 for the end. A line has no inside, so it needs a stroke to be visible.
points, a list of x and y pairs. A polygon closes the shape with a line from the last point to the first one.

image.alt: A rounded rectangle, a circle, an ellipse and a triangle in a row, with a wavy blue curve and a short brown line below them.

stepxmp.pre: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="320" height="140" viewBox="0 0 320 140"> <rect x="10" y="10" width="70" height="50" rx="10" fill="#cfe3f5" stroke="#1d4f7a" stroke-width="2"/> <circle cx="125" cy="35" r="25" fill="#f5e6c8" stroke="#7a4a10" stroke-width="2"/> <ellipse cx="195" cy="35" rx="35" ry="22" fill="#d9ecd0" stroke="#2f6b1f" stroke-width="2"/> <polygon points="250,60 275,10 300,60" fill="#f2d4d4" stroke="#8a2a2a" stroke-width="2"/> <path d="M10 110 C 50 80, 90 140, 130 110 S 210 80, 250 110" fill="none" stroke="#1d4f7a" stroke-width="3"/> <line x1="265" y1="95" x2="305" y2="125" stroke="#7a4a10" stroke-width="3"/> </svg>

step.cmd: Write the data of a path

info.p: The d attribute is a list of commands, each one with its numbers. A command in capital letters uses absolute coordinates. The same command in lowercase letters uses coordinates relative to the current point:

row.entry: Starts a new part of the path at a point, without drawing.
Draws a straight line to a point.
Draws a horizontal or a vertical line.
x1 y1 x2 y2 x y
Draws a cubic Bézier curve with two control points.
Draws a cubic curve that continues the previous curve smoothly.
Draws a quadratic Bézier curve with one control point.
Draws a quadratic curve that continues the previous curve smoothly.
rx ry rotation large-arc sweep x y
Draws an arc of an ellipse. The two flags, 0 or 1, choose which of the four possible arcs is drawn.
Closes the current part with a line to its start.

info.p: If the data has an error, CSSMedia draws the path up to the command before the error and ignores the rest.

A g element groups shapes. The properties you set on the group, such as fill, are inherited by the shapes inside it. The transform attribute moves, turns or scales the group and everything in it. It is a list of these functions:

ul.li: scale(x y) enlarges or reduces it. With one number, the scale is the same in both directions.
rotate(angle) turns it by an angle in degrees, around the origin of the drawing. rotate(angle x y) turns it around the point x y.
matrix(a b c d e f) gives the six numbers of the transform directly.

info.p: The CSS property transform does the same with CSS syntax: transform: translate(40px, 20px) rotate(15deg). You can also use the properties rotate, scale and translate and the 3D functions such as rotateY() and perspective(). The origin of a transform in a drawing is the origin of the drawing. Set transform-origin to turn an element around another point:

step.cmd: Define a shape once and draw it many times

info.p: Elements inside defs are not drawn. Give them an id, then draw them with a use element. Its href names the shape, and its x and y move the copy. The copy takes its style from the use element where the shape does not set its own, so each copy can have another color:

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <rect id="cell" width="20" height="20"/> </defs> <use href="#cell" x="0" y="0" fill="#cfe3f5"/> <use href="#cell" x="30" y="0" fill="#f5e6c8"/>

info.p: A symbol is a shape that has its own viewBox. It is never drawn by itself, and a use element that gives it a width and a height draws it scaled to that size. A use element can name an element of another drawing of your document too.

step.cmd: Draw the first alternative that applies

info.p: A switch element draws only its first child that has neither the systemLanguage nor the requiredExtensions attribute. CSSMedia supports no extension and has no language preference, so the children with these attributes never apply. Put the fallback last, without them.

An svg element inside a drawing makes a nested drawing. Its x, y, width and height place it, and its viewBox scales its content. What it draws outside its box is cut, unless you set overflow: visible.
With display: none an element and its children are not drawn. With visibility: hidden an element is not painted, but its children can still be visible when they set visibility: visible.
